profile.name: Bappa Ghosh
bio: I am a postdoctoral researcher in Biomedical Sciences at the University of North Dakota, studying how chromatin organization shapes gene regulation. My work combines sequencing, computational genomics, statistical modeling, and molecular simulation.

Trained in computational and theoretical biophysics, I work across cancer epigenetics, polymer dynamics, and biotechnology innovation. I also teach bioinformatics and contribute to the Detectology program.

researchCategories.title: Epigenetics, Bioinformatics & 3D Chromatin
researchCategories.description: I study how three-dimensional genome organization and pioneer transcription factors influence gene regulation in cancer. My work combines nanopore-based multiway chromatin contacts, Hi-C, chromatin accessibility, and transcriptomics. I develop computational workflows to quantify genome reorganization and connect chromatin structure with gene expression. I also study cell-free DNA and interpretable machine learning for cancer-related applications.

researchCategories.title: Polymer Dynamics & Molecular Simulation
researchCategories.description: My research uses statistical mechanics, molecular simulation, and computational biophysics to investigate the dynamics of complex systems. I have studied driven polymer translocation through nanopores, polymer–pore interactions, and the effects of charge and pH. Related work examines the behavior of active fluids, molecular assemblies, and nonequilibrium processes.

researchCategories.title: Innovation Activities
researchCategories.description: As Program Lead at Detectology, I support the development of accessible cell-free DNA extraction and analysis approaches for cancer-related applications. My activities include customer discovery, prototyping, translational research, and commercialization planning. Detectology has secured a reported combined $55,000 through Innovate ND and the UND Innovation Moonshot initiative.
